question: How strongly do each watch participant-level average heart rate and its concurrent ECG reference co-vary, and how far do they disagree in bpm?
unit_evidence: Workbook has 22 participant rows, no HR activity or timestamp columns; article Fig3 calls these average heart rate.
import: readxl; A1:M23 as text to preserve original duplicate header names; parse by explicit column map after header validation

reference_header_exception.evidence: Key Worksheet_4 explicitly defines this column as electrocardiography heart rate; article reference methods agrees

selection: Keep every finite participant-watch reference/device pair; report and retain invalid entries separately; stop if observed counts differ from 22 per device for investigation.
forbidden: joining HR to unrelated activity rows
primary: per-device scatter with OLS and identity y=x
OLS device=intercept+slope*ECG with coefficient t CI and R2
bounded_diagnostics: Spearman rank correlation as labelled secondary
classical descriptive Bland-Altman mean +/-1.96SD; no claim to reproduce regression-adjusted paper LoA
leave-one-participant-out sensitivity: 22 deletions per device; does not change primary sample
comparison_policy: Published results visible during source reading; not blinded. Compare after fit; never tune to targets. Original paper contains Pearson/Spearman and regression-dependent LoA, so metric differences need interpretation.
inference: Each per-device analysis uses 22 people. Devices share participants; no pooled n=88 independent-person p-value and no unpaired device superiority test.
validation: same-agent formula checks and R vs Python numpy/OpenPyXL cross-check; not external or independent-agent review
scope_limit: Heart_Rate assignment only. No energy expenditure, steps, ICC replication, subgroup search or nonexistent HR activity/time series.
completion: all four devices analysed on complete available HR data; each stage MD + four device MD; one final self-contained HTML with all plots, all 88 rows, issues and limitations
review_policy: data/code changes rerun dependent statistics; narrative-only changes review affected wording; style-only changes visual check; immutable run IDs
progress_cost_policy: log wall time, artifact sizes and failures; use short summaries; token/dollar telemetry unavailable; source checks stop after official paper, workbook Key and slides.
